On the interpretation of His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it" (16), "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation" (17), "So when We have recited it, follow its recitation" (18), "Then indeed upon Us is its explanation" (19):

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not move your tongue, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an, to hasten with it.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the reason for which he was told, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." Some of them said: He was told this because whenever something was revealed to him, he would hasten to it, desiring to memorize it out of his love for it, so he was told: Do not hasten with it, for We shall preserve it for you.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever the Qur'an was revealed to him would hasten, desiring to memorize it. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Like this," and he moved his lips.

⁕ 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari and Yunus narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever the Qur'an was revealed to him would hasten with it, desiring to memorize it. Yunus said: He would move his lips in order to memorize it, so Allah revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it, and he said regarding "Do not move your tongue with it": "Like this," and Sufyan moved his mouth.

⁕ Sufyan ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it": He said: When Jibril came down to him with the revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) would move his tongue and lips with it, and this would be difficult for him, and he would be recognized as doing so. So Allah revealed this verse in "I swear by the Day of Resurrection": "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whenever the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), he would move his lips, and he was recognized by that. Sa'id imitated it, and said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: To hasten in taking it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: Jibril (peace be upon him) would come down with the Qur'an, and he would move his tongue with it, hastening with it, so He said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Rab'i ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi regarding this verse: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: When the revelation came down to him, he would hasten to speak it out of his love for it, so it was revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it": Do not speak what We have revealed to you until its revelation is completed to you; and when We have completed its revelation to you, then speak it.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it": When the Qur'anic revelation came down to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), he would move his tongue with it, fearing that he would forget it.

Others said: Rather, the reason for which he was told this was that he used to recite the Qur'an frequently, fearing that he would forget it, so he was told: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is that We collect it for you and make you recite it, so you will not forget."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it": He would not cease from the Qur'an, fearing that he would forget it, so Allah said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is that We collect it for you," "and its recitation": that We make you recite it, so you will not forget.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it." He said: He would go over the Qur'an to recall it, fearing forgetfulness, so He said to him: "We have sufficed it for you, O Muhammad."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would move his tongue with it to recall it, so Allah said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, We shall preserve it for you."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) would move his tongue with it, fearing forgetfulness, so Allah revealed what you hear.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, "Do not move your tongue with it": He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recite the Qur'an and repeat it frequently, fearing that he would forget it.

The most likely of the two views in light of what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the view reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, because His words, "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation," indicate that He only forbade moving the tongue with it in haste before its collection; and it is known that his studying it to recall it would take place after Allah had gathered for him what he would study of it.

* *

As for His words: "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation":

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, upon Us is the collecting of this Qur'an in your breast, O Muhammad, until We fix it therein, "and its recitation": that is, and its recitation, so that you recite it after We have collected it in your breast.

The people of ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed, upon Us is its collection": He said: in your breast. "And its recitation": He said: that you recite it afterward.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation": that We collect it for you, "and its recitation": that We make you recite it, so you will not forget.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation": He says: Indeed, upon Us is that We collect it for you until We fix it in your heart.

Others interpreted His words "and its recitation" as "and its composition." The meaning of the speech for them was: Indeed, upon Us is its collection in your heart until you memorize it and its composition.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation": He means its memorization and its composition.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "Its collection and its recitation": He said: its memorization and its composition. Qatadah directed the meaning of "qur'an" to being a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "This she-camel has recited a fetus in her belly," when she gathers her womb around an offspring, as 'Amr ibn Kulthum said:

On the interpretation of His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it" (16), "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation" (17), "So when We have recited it, follow its recitation" (18), "Then indeed upon Us is its explanation" (19):

Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not move your tongue, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an, to hasten with it.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the reason for which he was told, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." Some of them said: He was told this because whenever something was revealed to him, he would hasten to it, desiring to memorize it out of his love for it, so he was told: Do not hasten with it, for We shall preserve it for you.

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever the Qur'an was revealed to him would hasten, desiring to memorize it. So Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation." Ibn 'Abbas said: "Like this," and he moved his lips.

⁕ 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari and Yunus narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that the Prophet (ﷺ) whenever the Qur'an was revealed to him would hasten with it, desiring to memorize it. Yunus said: He would move his lips in order to memorize it, so Allah revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ 'Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Habbari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it, and he said regarding "Do not move your tongue with it": "Like this," and Sufyan moved his mouth.

⁕ Sufyan ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it": He said: When Jibril came down to him with the revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) would move his tongue and lips with it, and this would be difficult for him, and he would be recognized as doing so. So Allah revealed this verse in "I swear by the Day of Resurrection": "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Whenever the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ), he would move his lips, and he was recognized by that. Sa'id imitated it, and said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: To hasten in taking it.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: Jibril (peace be upon him) would come down with the Qur'an, and he would move his tongue with it, hastening with it, so He said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Rab'i ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi regarding this verse: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: When the revelation came down to him, he would hasten to speak it out of his love for it, so it was revealed: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it": Do not speak what We have revealed to you until its revelation is completed to you; and when We have completed its revelation to you, then speak it.

⁕ It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it": When the Qur'anic revelation came down to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), he would move his tongue with it, fearing that he would forget it.

Others said: Rather, the reason for which he was told this was that he used to recite the Qur'an frequently, fearing that he would forget it, so he was told: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is that We collect it for you and make you recite it, so you will not forget."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it": He would not cease from the Qur'an, fearing that he would forget it, so Allah said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, upon Us is that We collect it for you," "and its recitation": that We make you recite it, so you will not forget.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it." He said: He would go over the Qur'an to recall it, fearing forgetfulness, so He said to him: "We have sufficed it for you, O Muhammad."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would move his tongue with it to recall it, so Allah said: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it. Indeed, We shall preserve it for you."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Do not move your tongue with it, to hasten with it." He said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) would move his tongue with it, fearing forgetfulness, so Allah revealed what you hear.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, "Do not move your tongue with it": He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recite the Qur'an and repeat it frequently, fearing that he would forget it.

The most likely of the two views in light of what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates is the view reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, because His words, "Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation," indicate that He only forbade moving the tongue with it in haste before its collection; and it is known that his studying it to recall it would take place after Allah had gathered for him what he would study of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 20–25:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Nay, but you love the hasty life (20) and neglect the Hereafter (21). Faces that Day will be radiant (22), looking toward their Lord (23). And faces that Day will be gloomy (24), thinking that a calamity is about to befall them (25).﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His servants addressed by this Qur'an, who prefer the adornment of the worldly life over the Hereafter: The matter is not as you say, O people, that you will not be resurrected after your death and will not be recompensed for your deeds. Rather, what prompted you to say that is your love of the hasty world and your preference for its desires over the deferred Hereafter and its bliss. You believe in the hasty life and deny the deferred one.

As for:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Nay, but you love the hasty life and neglect the Hereafter﴾: most people chose the hasty life, except those whom Allah has shown mercy and protected.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Faces on that Day, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, will be radiant: that is, good and beautiful from bliss. It is said of this: "Nadara wajh fulan" (the face of so-and-so became radiant) when it became beautiful from blessing; and "Nadhdhara Allah wajhahu" (Allah made his face radiant) when He made it beautiful in the same way.

The interpreters differed regarding this. Some of them said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: beautiful.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: the radiance of the faces is their beauty.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: the radiant ones: the blessed ones.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: the beautiful faces.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: from joy, bliss and delight.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they are joyful.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: joyful. ﴿Looking toward their Lord﴾.

The interpreters differed regarding the explanation of that. Some of them said: the meaning of that is that they look toward their Lord.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Tusi and Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, both saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, who said: ﴿Looking toward their Lord, gazing﴾.

* Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed me regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾ from bliss ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: Yazid al-Nahwi informed me, from Ikrimah and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, and shaykhs from the people of Kufa, who said: They look toward their Lord, gazing.

* Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: al-Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: beautiful. ﴿Looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they look toward the Creator, and it is right that they be radiant while looking toward the Creator.

* Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu Arfajah narrated to us, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: They look toward Allah; their eyes cannot encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them. This is His saying: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [6:103].

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they await the reward from their Lord.

Mention of those who said that:

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await reward from Him.

* He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await the reward from their Lord.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await the reward.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await the reward from their Lord; nothing among His creation sees Him.

* Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾: he said: radiance from bliss. ﴿Looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await His provision and His bounty.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: some people used to say, concerning the hadith "They will see their Lord": I said to Mujahid: Some people say that He is seen. He said: He sees, and nothing sees Him.

* He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await from their Lord what He has commanded for them.

* Abu al-Khattab al-Hassani narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to us, from Sufyan, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾: he said: they await the reward.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Thuwayr, from Mujahid, from Ibn Umar, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his kingdom, his thrones and his servants for a distance of a thousand years; he sees its farthest point as he sees its nearest. And the highest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon the Face of Allah morning and evening."

* He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ashja' narrated to us, from Abu al-Sahba' al-Mawsili, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who sees his thrones, his servants and his kingdom at a distance of a thousand years, so he sees its farthest point as he sees its nearest. And the most excellent of them in rank is the one who looks upon the Face of Allah at dawn and dusk."

The most correct of the two opinions in our view is the one we mentioned from al-Hasan and Ikrimah, that the meaning is that they look toward their Creator. This is also what has come in the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

* Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Abjar narrated to me, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Thuwayr, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his kingdom for two thousand years. And the most excellent of them in rank is the one who looks upon the Face of Allah twice every day." He said: Then he recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, [and] said: "With whiteness and clarity." He said: ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: "they look every day upon the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

* He said: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Ashja' narrated to us, from Abu al-Sahba' al-Mawsili, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who sees his thrones, his servants and his kingdom at a distance of a thousand years, so he sees its farthest point as he sees its nearest. And the most excellent of them in rank is the one who looks upon the Face of Allah at dawn and dusk."

The most correct of the two opinions in our view is the one we mentioned from al-Hasan and Ikrimah, that the meaning is that they look toward their Creator. This is also what has come in the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

* Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Abjar narrated to me, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Isra'il ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Thuwayr, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who looks upon his kingdom for two thousand years. And the most excellent of them in rank is the one who looks upon the Face of Allah twice every day." He said: Then he recited: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾, [and] said: "With whiteness and clarity." He said: ﴿looking toward their Lord﴾: "they look every day upon the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

* *

And His saying: ﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And faces on that Day will be changed in color, darkened and frowning. It is said: "Basara wajhahu, absuruhu basran" when one does that, and "basara wajhuhu, fahuwa basir, bayyin al-busur" (his face was gloomy; he is gloomy, clearly gloomy).

The interpreters said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿gloomy﴾: he said: scowling.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾: i.e., frowning.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿gloomy﴾: he said: scowling.

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿gloomy﴾: he said: scowling.

* *

And His saying: ﴿thinking that a calamity is about to befall them﴾

He, the Exalted, says: they know that a calamity will befall them. Al-faqirah means a calamity.

The interpreters said in accordance with what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿thinking that a calamity is about to befall them﴾: he said: a calamity.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿thinking that a calamity is about to befall them﴾: i.e., evil.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿thinking that a calamity is about to befall them﴾: he said: they think they will enter the Fire. He said: That is the calamity. The origin of al-faqirah is the branding mark placed on the nose (al-wasm alladhi yufqaru bihi 'ala al-anf).

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nay, when it reaches the collarbones﴾ [75:26] and what follows.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The matter is not as these polytheists imagine, that they will not be punished for their polytheism and their disobedience to their Lord. Rather, when the soul of one of them reaches the collarbones at the time of his death, and the rattle sets in.

Ibn Zayd said, concerning God's saying ﴿Nay, when it reaches the collarbones﴾: "The collarbones: his soul."

⁕ Yunus related this to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾ [75:27]: He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: his family said, "Who will charm him to heal him from what has befallen him?" They sought for him physicians and healers, but they availed him nothing against the command of God that had come upon him.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿Who is a reciter?﴾. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah: ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾ He said: "Is there anyone who will recite (charms)?"

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Shabib, from Abu Qilabah: ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾ He said: "Is there any healing physician?"

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Shabib, from Abu Qilabah, the like of it.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah related to us, from Abu Bistam, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning God's saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾ He said: "He is the physician."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak concerning ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾. He said: "Is there any healer?"

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾, meaning: they sought physicians for him, but they availed him nothing against the decree of God.

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Yazid said concerning His saying ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾: "Where are the physicians, and the reciters: who will charm him from death?"

Others said: Rather, this is the saying of the angels to one another, one of them saying to another: "Who will ascend with it (the soul)?"

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, saying: My father related to me, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Nay, when it reaches the collarbones, and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾. He said: "When his soul reaches (the throat), it is 'charmed' (raised) with it. The angels say: 'Who will ascend with it, the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment?'"

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, concerning His saying ﴿and it is said, "Who is a reciter?"﴾. He said: "It reached me from Abu Qilabah that he said: 'Is there any physician?'" He said: "And it reached me from Abu al-Jawza' that he said: The angels said to one another: 'Who will raise it? The angels of mercy or the angels of punishment?'"

* *

And His saying: ﴿and he thought that it was parting﴾ [75:28].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: The one upon whom that has descended became certain that it was the parting from the world, from family, wealth and children.

The people of ta'wil said something similar to what we have said regarding that.

Those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and he thought that it was parting﴾, meaning: he was certain that it was parting.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and he thought that it was parting﴾: "None of God's creatures can repel death, nor deny it. But he does not know whether he will die from that illness or from something else. So the 'thought' here is this."

* *

And His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾ [75:29].

The people of ta'wil differed concerning the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: the severity of the affairs of this world was entwined with the severity of the affairs of the Hereafter.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham related to us, saying: My father related to me, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "The severity of this world with the Hereafter."

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He says: "The last day of this world and the first day of the Hereafter, so severity meets severity, except for the one whom God has mercy upon."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He says: "The world was entwined with the Hereafter, and that is the shin of the world and the Hereafter. Have you not heard that He says: ﴿To your Lord on that day is the driving﴾ [75:30]?"

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "The affair of this world was entwined with the affair of the Hereafter at death."

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, who said: "The last day of this world, and the first day of the Hereafter."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: Al-Hasan said: "The shin of this world with the Hereafter."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Mujahid, who said: "It is the affair of this world and the Hereafter at death."

⁕ 'Ali ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak concerning His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "The people of this world prepare the body, and the people of the Hereafter prepare the soul."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Two matters gathered upon him: people prepare his body, and the angels prepare his soul."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: al-Muharibi related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The shin of this world with the shin of the Hereafter."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', the like of it, and he added: "It is said: their entwining is at death."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah, who said: "The world and the Hereafter."

⁕ He said: Ibn Yaman related to us, from 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid, from his father, who said: "The affair of this world with the affair of the Hereafter."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "The affair of this world with the affair of the Hereafter."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "Severity with severity, the shin of this world with the shin of the Hereafter."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: I asked Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, and he said: "The work of this world with the work of the Hereafter."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Salamah, from al-Dahhak, who said: "They are the world and the Hereafter."

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾: "The scholars say about it two sayings: among them is one who says: the shin of the Hereafter with the shin of this world."

Others said: "Rarely does a dead person die except that one of his shins is entwined with the other." Ibn Zayd said: "Yet we have no doubt that it is the shin of the Hereafter," and he recited: ﴿To your Lord on that day is the driving﴾. He said: "When the Hereafter is entwined with this world, the driving is to God." He said: "And this is the most common view of those who say that."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the two shins of the dead person were entwined when they were wrapped in the shroud.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Muhajir related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "He wrapped them in the shroud."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Waki' and Ibn al-Yaman related to us, from Bishr ibn al-Muhajir, from al-Hasan, who said: "They are your two shins when they are wrapped in the shroud."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Bishr ibn al-Muhajir, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: the entwining of the dead person's two shins at death.

Those who said that:

⁕ Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Amir: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "The two shins of the dead."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab and 'Abd al-A'la related to us, both saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Amir, who said: "His two shins were entwined at death."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to me, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, the like of it.

⁕ Ishaq ibn Shahin related to me, saying: Khalid related to us, from Dawud, from 'Amir, in a similar manner.

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "At death."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: "Your two shins were entwined at death."

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. "The command of God entwined them."

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, who said: al-Hasan said: "The two shins of the son of Adam at death."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "They are his two shins when one is pressed against the other."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. Qatadah said: "Did you not see him when he strikes his leg against the other leg?"

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. "His two legs die, so they no longer carry him anywhere, though they used to carry him about."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "His two shins at death."

Others said: What is meant by that is: their becoming dry at death.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "Their drying at death."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

Others said: The meaning of that is: "and an affair was entwined with an affair."

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu 'Isa: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "An affair with an affair."

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is: "and a trial was entwined with a trial."

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: "A trial with a trial."

The most correct of the sayings in this matter in my view is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: "and the shin of this world was entwined with the shin of the Hereafter," and that is the severity of the agony of death with the severity of the terror of the place of arrival. What indicates that this is its interpretation is His saying: ﴿To your Lord on that day is the driving﴾. The Arabs say of every matter that has become severe: "He has girded up his shin," and "He has uncovered his shin." And from it is the saying of the poet:

When she hitches up her shin for you,
Then it is spring, so do not tire.

[Footnote in the printed edition: In the printed text it reads "idha wa-akhar" [in place of "idha shammarat"?]. His saying "fa-rafa' al-ism" means what is in Labid's verse "thumma ism", and it should have been in the accusative as an incitement, had he said "thumma 'alaykuma ism al-salam" with the incitement placed first.]

By His saying ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾ is meant: one of the two severities became joined to the other, just as it is said of a woman when one of her thighs is pressed against the other: "laffa'" (she has pressed her thighs together).

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "They are his two shins when one is pressed against the other."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. Qatadah said: "Did you not see him when he strikes his leg against the other leg?"

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. "His two legs die, so they no longer carry him anywhere, though they used to carry him about."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "His two shins at death."

Others said: What is meant by that is: their becoming dry at death.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "Their drying at death."

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

Others said: The meaning of that is: "and an affair was entwined with an affair."

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb and Abu Hisham related to us, both saying: Waki' related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Abu 'Isa: ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾. He said: "An affair with an affair."

Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is: "and a trial was entwined with a trial."

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Hisham related to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, who said: "A trial with a trial."

The most correct of the sayings in this matter in my view is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: "and the shin of this world was entwined with the shin of the Hereafter," and that is the severity of the agony of death with the severity of the terror of the place of arrival. What indicates that this is its interpretation is His saying: ﴿To your Lord on that day is the driving﴾. The Arabs say of every matter that has become severe: "He has girded up his shin," and "He has uncovered his shin." And from it is the saying of the poet:

When she hitches up her shin for you,
Then it is spring, so do not tire.

[Footnote in the printed edition: In the printed text it reads "idha wa-akhar" [in place of "idha shammarat"?]. His saying "fa-rafa' al-ism" means what is in Labid's verse "thumma ism", and it should have been in the accusative as an incitement, had he said "thumma 'alaykuma ism al-salam" with the incitement placed first.]

By His saying ﴿and the shin was entwined with the shin﴾ is meant: one of the two severities became joined to the other, just as it is said of a woman when one of her thighs is pressed against the other: "laffa'" (she has pressed her thighs together).

* *

And His saying: ﴿To your Lord on that day is the driving﴾.

He says: To your Lord, O Muhammad, on the day when the shin is entwined with the shin, is the driving.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 75, verses 31–36:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. Then he went to his family, swaggering.(33) Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!(35) Does man think that he will be left aimless?﴾

Exalted is He, says: He did not believe in the Book of Allah, nor did he pray to Him, but he denied the Book of Allah and turned away, disobeying Allah.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed﴾: he did not believe in the Book of Allah, nor did he pray to Allah. ﴿But denied and turned away﴾: he denied the Book of Allah and turned away from the obedience of Allah.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾

Exalted is He, says: then he went off to his family, returning to them, strutting in his walk.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾: i.e., strutting.

Sa'id ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from Maysarah ibn 'Ubayd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His words ﴿Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾, he said: strutting; it is the gait of the Banu Makhzum.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿went to his family, swaggering﴾, he said: He saw a man of Quraysh walking, and said: "This is how he used to walk, just as this one walks, strutting."

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿swaggering﴾, he said: strutting, and it was Abu Jahl ibn Hisham; that was his gait.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿swaggering﴾, he said: Abu Jahl.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So he neither believed nor prayed, but denied and turned away. Then he went to his family, swaggering﴾: this refers to Abu Jahl, strutting proudly.

What is meant by His words ﴿yatamattha﴾ is that he twists his back (mata) in pride, and the mata is the back; from this is the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "When my community walks the mutayta'," and that is when a man throws his arms out and sways.

* *

This is a threat from Allah upon a threat to Abu Jahl.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Woe to you, and woe! Again, woe to you, and woe!﴾: a threat upon a threat, as you hear. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 75, verse 37–40:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted (in an emission)?

Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾

Says He, may He be remembered: Did this denier not have (the knowledge that) God is able to bring him back to life after his death, and to create him anew after his annihilation? ﴿A drop﴾ means: a small amount of water in the loins of a man, of semen.

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿yumna (يُمْنَى)﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read ﴿tumna (تُمْنَى)﴾ with a "t", meaning: the drop is emitted. Some of the reciters of Mecca and Basra read ﴿yumna (يُمْنَى)﴾ with a "y", meaning: the semen is emitted.

The correct view is that both are well-known recitations with sound meanings, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct.

Says He, may He be remembered: then he became blood after having been a drop, then a clot, then He proportioned him as a complete human being, speaking, hearing, seeing. ﴿And made of him two mates, the male and the female﴾ means: He made from this human, after proportioning him into a well-formed creation, children for him, males and females. ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ means: Is not the One who did that, creating this human from a drop, then a clot, until He made him a complete human being who has male and female children, able to bring the dead back to life from their death, so that He causes them to exist again as they were before their death?

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Is not He able to give life to the dead?﴾ It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited it, would say: "Glory be to You, and yes (bala)."

End of the commentary on Surah al-Qiyamah.
